lore_content:
Dearest Traveler,

Tohoku is a region where the past is not remembered, but felt. Walking along the ancient cedar paths of Dewa Sanzan, beneath trees that have stood for a thousand years, one feels the persistent, moss-covered breath of history. This is the land of spirits, mountain ascetics (Yamabushi), and hidden waterfalls.

In the spring, the cherry blossoms of Hirosaki Castle drape over the ancient stone walls like heavy silk, their petals falling into the emerald moats below. And in the dark of August, the giant lantern floats of the Nebuta Festival pierce the night, carrying the roaring courage of warriors into the summer breeze. Tohoku reminds us that our roots must run deep to withstand the storms of life.

With enduring warmth,
Kokoro of Tohoku
